current.summary: One open living and dining room under the exposed roof: dark beams and rafters with a weathered boarded deck, sloping down over the dining end. Warm white plastered walls. Sitting area: grey sofa (2.1 m) facing a wall-mounted TV; under the TV a 1950s painted sideboard on hairpin legs, above it a timber shelf with trailing plants; a trunk covered with a tapestry serves as coffee table. Behind the sofa, the stepped white masonry: a daybed niche with dark cushions, and above it the high ledge with a row of recesses under the cut-off old beam stubs — each recess now has a white up/down wall light. An arched opening (black sheet for now) leads to the kitchen. Dining end: dark extendable table with four green velvet chairs, a tall dark-wood dresser (wine and display), and the two old olive-green built-in cupboards — one glazed (china), one panelled with a paint-strip test patch and a raw open recess above it used as a shelf. Between dining and back doors: the exposed brick panel with a wall light over the antique bar counter. Back doors (wood, glazed, with wooden shutters) sit in a recess and open onto a small balcony; front doors with internal shutters open onto the front terrace. Also: gilt mirror over a wrought-iron wine-rack console, brass and glass-drop chandelier, cage pendants. Floor: large light-grey tiles.

target.concept: The room is largely there: exposed roof, lit recesses, daybed nook, olive-green cupboards, antiques. Target is to finish it — the attic ledge tiled and given a slim rail, the timbers sealed, the walls in one warm white, the cupboards completed in their olive green, a proper top on the TV unit, and the loose cables and unfinished corners tidied.

target.renderPrompt:
Edit this photo of a room in our house. Keep the exact camera angle and keep all the architecture exactly as it is — walls, room shape, windows, doors, beams, floor and fixed fittings. Do not add, move or remove anything structural, and do not change the furniture unless I say so below. Remove all clutter: tools, boxes, bags, dust sheets, loose cables, packaging, laundry and toiletries. Show the room finished and tidy.

Changes to make:
- Keep the furniture and lights exactly as they are: grey sofa, tapestry trunk, painted sideboard under the TV, gilt mirror, chandelier, cage pendants, the white up/down lights in the recesses.
- Walls freshly painted warm white. The old roof beams and boards are clean with a matt finish, not glossy.
- The raised attic ledge above the daybed is tiled in the same light grey floor tiles, with a slim black wrought-iron balustrade along its edge (plain vertical bars, about 1 m high), a few floor cushions and a lantern up there.
- The daybed nook has neat fitted cushions and one small brass wall light.
- The sideboard under the TV has a solid oak top.
- The arched opening is open (no black sheet). No visible cables anywhere.

Style: photorealistic interior photograph, natural light plus warm 2700K lamps, no people, no text or labels.

scope: Electrics: nook light + socket, hide cables, finish back-door recess

surfaces.prep: Check the ledge is solid, level and can carry people (it will be used as a sitting area) — builder to confirm. Fix the balustrade posts first so tiles are cut round them
surfaces.finish: Tile with flexible adhesive, edge nosing along the front
surfaces.colour: Light-grey floor tile, as the rest of the floor

surfaces.prep: Brush and vacuum; check for woodworm (small round holes, fresh dust) and treat with a clear woodworm treatment if found; mask walls
surfaces.finish: 2 coats clear matt hardwax-oil or matt water-based varnish
surfaces.notes: Check roof insulation above the boards before sealing. Do this before painting walls — it drips

surfaces.prep: Make good rough patches (recess on the ledge, above the recess by the arch, back-door recess, around the cupboards), fill, sand, spot-prime
surfaces.notes: Cut in carefully around the brick panel and beam stubs — leave both unpainted

surfaces.prep: Clean, light sand, touch in the stripped patch
surfaces.finish: 2 coats Magic Paint Italy olive green, then its clear protective finish

notes: Order: electrics first-fix (nook light, socket, hidden cables, back-door recess) → balustrade fixings → tile the ledge → timbers → make good and paint walls → cupboards → TV unit top
